bucket_config.description: Configuration schema for a data bucket specifying how data is sourced and updated. This schema supports multiple source types including devices and MQTT topics, each with its own set of required properties.

device.description: The unique identifier for the device.

interval.description: The time between updates, in seconds.

resource.description: The specific resource from the device being tracked.

source.description: Indicates the data source is a device.

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

update.description: Specifies that the bucket is updated at regular intervals.

user.description: The unique identifier for the user associated with this bucket.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data sourced from a device with event-based or no updates. This variation does not require an interval.

device.description: The unique identifier for the device.

resource.description: The specific resource from the device being tracked.

source.description: Indicates the data source is a device.

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

update.description: Specifies how the bucket is updated: either by specific events or not updated automatically.

user.description: The unique identifier for the user associated with this bucket.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data sourced from an MQTT topic. This requires specifying the topic and allows optional tags.

source.description: Indicates the data source is an MQTT topic.

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

topic.description: The MQTT topic from which data is sourced.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data manually written or provided via an API. This variation only requires source specification and allows optional tags.

source.description: Indicates the data source is either manually written ('write') or sourced via an API ('api').

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the retention period.

product_conditional_icon.title: Product Conditional Icon

type.description: Product type that determines the device status view

product_profile_category.description: Every entry of a category, by id. Replaces the whole category: entries missing from the body are removed (for properties, also the default property on the devices).
product_profile_category.title: Product profile category

product_profile_code.description: JavaScript run by the server for this product: functions referenced by payload_function, device_id_resolver and function targets. Inline in `code`, or the files of a file storage in `storage` (takes precedence): its `index.js`, or `<path>/index.js` with `path`, so one storage can hold a whole application (dashboard, product code…).

path.description: Folder of the storage with the code (its index.js and node_modules), relative to the storage root, e.g. "code/meter". Empty: the storage root.

storage.description: File storage id with the product code.

product_profile_code.title: Product profile code

product_profile_entry.description: One entry of a product profile category; its id is the {resource} path parameter (or the key in a category body). Entries only run when `enabled` is true. Fields by category. properties: `data` fills the device property of the same id (optional), `default.value` / `form` / `perm` / `type` create it on every device of the product. buckets: `data` writes into the bucket with the entry id, created on the first write; an id containing {{device}} gives one bucket per device (such ids only fit the whole-category PUT, as the {resource} path parameter cannot hold braces), otherwise one shared bucket tagged with device (and group); `tags`, `backend`, `retention`. flows: `data` → `sink`, `split_data` sends each array element separately. api: resources added to every device of the product: `request.data` (target), `response.data` (response), `device_id_resolver` (function of the product code that returns the device id from the payload, needed to call the resource through POST /products/{product}/resources/{resource}), `handle_connectivity` (validate / auto-provision the device on calls; default true for resource_stream targets). autoprovisions: `config`. endpoints: deprecated, use flows with an endpoint_call sink.

backend.description: buckets: storage backend of the bucket when it is created (mongodb, influxdb, dynamodb; default the server's).

config.description: autoprovisions: when a device that does not exist authenticates or calls a resource and its id matches `pattern`, it is created in this product (HTTP, or Subdevice for MQTT), with asset `type` / `group` and `project` if given.

group.description: Asset group for the new devices.

pattern.description: Regular expression on the device id, e.g. ^meter_[0-9]{6}$.

type.description: Asset type for the new devices.

data.description: Data source, or an array of sources.

default.description: properties: initial property value on each device, in `value`.

form.description: properties: form used by the console to edit the value (`fields`).

retention.description: buckets: retention of the bucket when it is created.

tags.description: buckets: record fields stored as tags (filterable), e.g. ["line"].

product_profile_entry.title: Product profile entry

product_profile_payload_type.description: How the payload is built. template_payload (default): `payload` is a template that may use {{payload}}, {{payload.field}}, {{device}}, {{property.<name>}}, {{api.<resource>}} or {{meta.<device field>}}. source_payload: the data as received. source_event: the whole event (device, product, timestamps, payload…). none: no payload.

product_profile_response.description: What an API resource answers (`response.data`). `source` selects it: request_response: what the request target returned; topic → `topic`: wait for a message on that MQTT topic (from the same device, or any with `publish_source`: any); property → `property`; resource → `resource`; function → `function`; endpoint_call → `endpoint`; none. The answer can be shaped with `payload` / `payload_type` / `payload_function`.

payload.description: Template string (payload_type template_payload) or JSON value.

publish_source.description: source topic: empty (only the same device) or any.

source.description: request_response | topic | property | resource | function | endpoint_call | none

product_profile_response.title: Product profile API response

product_profile_source.description: Where a properties / buckets / flows entry gets its data. `source` selects the fields used: topic → `topic` (MQTT topic, + and # wildcards; {{name}} placeholders match one level, and in buckets each one becomes a tag of the record, with {{field}} naming the record field so several topics merge into one record); resource → `resource`, `update` (interval | events) with `interval` + `magnitude`; resource_stream → `resource_stream` (the device pushes it); product_stream → `product_stream`; event → `event` with optional `filter`. Only devices of this product are listened to. The received data can then be transformed with `payload_type` / `payload` and `payload_function`.

event.description: source event: server event name, e.g. device_state_change, device_property_update, bucket_write.

filter.description: source event: extra filters (event field: value or regex). The product filter is always added.

interval.description: source resource with update interval: number of `magnitude` units between reads, e.g. 60.

magnitude.description: second (default) | minute | hour | day | week | month | year

patch.description: properties only: merge the value into the device property instead of replacing it.

payload.description: Template string (payload_type template_payload) or JSON value.

payload_function.description: Name of a function of the product code that receives the payload and returns the value to use.

product_stream.description: source product_stream: stream published by an API resource or flow of this product (target product_stream).

resource.description: source resource: device resource read by the server.

resource_stream.description: source resource_stream: device resource the device streams on its own.

topic.description: source topic: MQTT topic of the device messages, e.g. devices/{{device}}/telemetry.

update.description: source resource: interval (default, read every `interval` `magnitude`) | events (the device streams it when it changes).

product_profile_source.title: Product profile data source

product_profile_target.description: What an API resource request (`request.data`) or a flow (`sink`) does. `target` selects the fields used: topic → `topic` (+ `retain`): publish to the device over MQTT; resource → `resource`: call a device resource (IOTMP devices); resource_stream → `resource_stream`; property → `property`: set a device property; function → `function`: run a function of the product code; endpoint_call → `endpoint`: call an endpoint; plugin_endpoint → `plugin` + `path`; product_stream → `product_stream` (and optional `product`): publish to a product stream; none. The body sent is built from `payload` / `payload_type` / `payload_function`. A target needs a device: the one in the URL, the source device, or the one returned by the entry's `device_id_resolver`.

endpoint.description: target endpoint_call: endpoint id (may use placeholders).

path.description: target plugin_endpoint: path inside the plugin, e.g. /api/process.

payload.description: Template string (payload_type template_payload) or JSON value.

retain.description: target topic: publish as a retained MQTT message.

target.description: topic | resource | resource_stream | property | function | endpoint_call | plugin_endpoint | product_stream | none

product_profile_target.title: Product profile target

product_service.description: A service the devices of the product expose, reached through the server: web (HTTP proxy) or vnc (remote desktop). The target is the address and port as seen from the device.
product_service.title: Product service

domain.description: Hostname to serve with its own TLS certificate, e.g. iot.example.com. Before verifying, point it to this server (A/AAAA record to its IP, or CNAME to its hostname) and make sure port 80 is reachable from the internet: POST /v1/domains/{domain}/verify gets a Let's Encrypt certificate through an HTTP-01 challenge (a *.wildcard needs the DNS-01 challenge, only on Thinger-hosted servers). Certificates renew automatically while the DNS keeps pointing here. Brand the console on it by creating a brand with the same id.

schema.description: Merged (RFC 7386 merge patch: null removes a key) into the host custom settings, on top of the provider settings. Changes apply after POST /v1/hosts/{host}/restart. On cloud instances (configured by a subscription), database, plugins, rate_limiter, http_server.hosts and accounts.limits.{accounts,brands,domains,members} belong to the plan: sending them returns 403, and stored ones are ignored.

schema.description: An alarm rule checks its data sources every check_interval and raises one alarm instance per device that meets the activation conditions. Sources: 'bucket' (bucket data, optionally aggregated and grouped by device), 'device_property' (a device property, resolved with type / group / product inheritance) and 'device_status' (connection.active, connection.ts). Sources can be narrowed with project, product, asset_type, asset_group or device. Conditions read '<source name>.<field>' and compare it with above, below, equal, not_equal (value), inside, outside (min, max), present or absent; values are strings, and can be expressions over other sources of the same device (e.g. 'limits.value.max_depth_m', a per-device threshold from a device_property source). device_property fields are paths in the property document: 'value.<field>'. Confirmation: immediate, sequence (N detections in a row) or timespan. Notifications call endpoints.
